content.introduction: The Federal Reserve cut interest rates by 25 basis points in its final decision of 2024, marking the third rate cut of the year. This decision aligns with market predictions of an overwhelmingly likely rate cut for the December meeting. The Fed's Summary of Economic Projections forecasts two interest-rate cuts for 2025. The interest-rate cut follows an uptick in inflation, with the consumer price index rising 2.7% year-over-year in November, signaling that the Federal Reserve may move more cautiously in the coming year.
body:
The nation's central bank cut interest rates in its final decision of 2024.

On Wednesday, the Federal Open Market Committee announced an interest-rate cut of 25 basis points, the third rate cut Americans have received this year. The decision fell in line with market predictions that estimated a rate cut was overwhelmingly likely for the Federal Reserve's December meeting. [...] The Fed's Summary of Economic Projections, released alongside the interest rate decision, also forecasts two interest-rate cuts for 2025.

The interest-rate cut comes one week after the latest inflation data — the consumer price index rose 2.7% year-over-year in November, an uptick from 2.6% in October and 2.4% in September. Accelerating inflation could signal that the Federal Reserve may move more cautiously in the coming year. [...] "There's the risk that we move too quickly and undermine the progress we've made on inflation, and there's the risk that we move too slowly and unnecessarily undermine the labor market," Fed Chair Jerome Powell said during The New York Times' DealBook conference on December 4. "And we're trying to be in that middle place and get it just right so that we continue to get inflation coming down. "
